name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

# Cancel in-progress runs on the same branch when a new push arrives.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true

jobs:
  # ── 1. Format ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  fmt:
    name: Format
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      # rustfmt is a pure Rust binary — no C toolchain needed.

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt

      - name: cargo fmt --check
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

  # ── 2. Clippy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  clippy:
    name: Clippy
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable
        with:
          components: clippy

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@42dc69e1aa15d09112580998cf2ef0119e2e91ae  # v2
        with:
          shared-key: clippy

      - name: cargo clippy — deny all warnings
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

  # ── 3. Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config musl-tools && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      # The wasm32 + tract-onnx + musl target combination produces a lot
      # of build output. Free space up-front and at the end so subsequent
      # jobs on the same runner aren't squeezed by leftover artefacts.
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          df -h
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/share/boost /usr/share/swift /usr/local/.ghcup \
            "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY:-/opt/hostedtoolcache}" 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo apt-get clean 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable
        with:
          targets: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl,wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@42dc69e1aa15d09112580998cf2ef0119e2e91ae  # v2
        with:
          shared-key: build

      # Build the ingredient-ai WASM crate first so the larderly crate's
      # `scanner-wasm` feature can `include_bytes!` the resulting module.
      - name: Install wasm-pack
        run: |
          if ! command -v wasm-pack >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            curl https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/installer/init.sh -sSf | sh -s -- -f
          fi
          wasm-pack --version

      - name: Build ingredient-ai WASM module
        run: make wasm-pack

      - name: cargo build — workspace (warnings as errors)
        run: RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build --workspace

      - name: cargo build — larderly with scanner-wasm feature
        run: RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build -p larderly --features scanner-wasm

      - name: cargo build — musl static target (with scanner-wasm)
        run: RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -p larderly --features scanner-wasm

  # ── 4. Rust tests ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  rust-tests:
    name: Rust Tests
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: [fmt, clippy]

    env:
      DATABASE_URL:          postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/larderly_github_${{ github.run_id }}_test
      SESSION_SECRET:        ci-test-session-secret-not-used-in-production-000000000000
      APP_BASE_URL:          http://localhost:3000
      S3_ENDPOINT:           ${{ vars.S3_ENDPOINT }}
      S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:      ${{ secrets.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
      S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:  ${{ secrets.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
      S3_ASSETS_BUCKET:      ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BUCKET }}
      S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET:     ${{ vars.S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET }}
      S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL:    ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL }}
      OIDC_MOCK:             "true"

    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config postgresql-client && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - name: Create test database
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_test;"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "CREATE DATABASE larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_test;"

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@42dc69e1aa15d09112580998cf2ef0119e2e91ae  # v2
        with:
          shared-key: rust-tests

      - name: Install sqlx-cli
        run: cargo install sqlx-cli --no-default-features --features rustls,postgres

      - name: Run migrations
        run: cargo sqlx migrate run

      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --workspace

      - name: Drop test database
        if: always()
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_test;" || true

  # ── 5. Playwright e2e ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  e2e:
    name: Playwright E2E
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: [rust-tests]

    env:
      DATABASE_URL:          postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/larderly_github_${{ github.run_id }}_e2e
      SESSION_SECRET:        ci-e2e-session-secret-not-used-in-production-000000000000
      APP_BASE_URL:          http://localhost:3001
      APP_PORT:              "3001"
      S3_ENDPOINT:           ${{ vars.S3_ENDPOINT }}
      S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:      ${{ secrets.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
      S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:  ${{ secrets.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
      S3_ASSETS_BUCKET:      ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BUCKET }}
      S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET:     ${{ vars.S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET }}
      S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL:    ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL }}
      OIDC_MOCK:             "true"
      # E2E runs ~80 tests sequentially from a single runner IP; the
      # default 30 mutations/min/ip would 429 mid-run. Effectively
      # disable the limit in CI — the limiter's behaviour itself is
      # covered by unit tests; the e2e job's job is the integration
      # glue. Per-test counts include retries (2x on failure) which
      # can push concurrent POSTs to surprising levels.
      RATE_LIMIT_MUTATIONS_PER_MIN: "100000"

    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config curl postgresql-client && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - name: Create test database
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_e2e;"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "CREATE DATABASE larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_e2e;"

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@42dc69e1aa15d09112580998cf2ef0119e2e91ae  # v2
        with:
          shared-key: e2e

      - name: Install sqlx-cli
        run: cargo install sqlx-cli --no-default-features --features rustls,postgres

      - name: Run migrations
        run: cargo sqlx migrate run

      # E2E tests mock the scanner module (the JS dynamic import 404s
      # gracefully and the page falls back to its stub). Building without
      # `--features scanner-wasm` saves a second wasm32 + tract-onnx
      # compile per CI run; the Build job already verifies the feature
      # builds cleanly.
      - name: Build app binary
        run: cargo build -p larderly

      - name: Start app
        run: |
          ./target/debug/larderly &
          echo $! > /tmp/larderly.pid
          echo -n "Waiting for app"
          until curl -sf http://localhost:3001/health > /dev/null 2>&1; do
            printf '.'
            sleep 1
          done
          echo " ready"

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: tests-e2e/package-lock.json

      - name: Install Playwright
        run: cd tests-e2e && npm ci && npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run Playwright tests
        run: cd tests-e2e && BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001 npx playwright test

      - name: Stop app
        if: always()
        run: kill $(cat /tmp/larderly.pid) 2>/dev/null || true

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: tests-e2e/playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Drop test database
        if: always()
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_e2e;" || true

  # ── 6. Container build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  container:
    name: Container Build
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: [build, rust-tests]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.base_ref == 'main'

    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y docker.io && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build scratch container
        run: DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 docker build -f Containerfile -t larderly:ci .

      - name: Smoke test — binary exists in image
        run: |
          # Verify /larderly is present in the scratch image by extracting it.
          # Running the binary directly requires env vars (config loads at startup),
          # so we check existence instead.
          docker create --name larderly-smoke larderly:ci
          docker cp larderly-smoke:/larderly /tmp/larderly-smoke
          docker rm larderly-smoke
          test -f /tmp/larderly-smoke
          echo "Binary is present in the container image"

name: Pull Request

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

# Cancel in-progress runs on the same PR when a new push arrives so we
# don't pay for stale coverage / scan jobs.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read

jobs:
  # ── 1. Test with coverage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Runs the full Rust test suite (unit + sqlx integration) against a real
  # PostgreSQL instance and collects LCOV coverage for SonarQube.
  test:
    name: Run Tests with Coverage
    runs-on: self-hosted

    env:
      DATABASE_URL:          postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/larderly_github_${{ github.run_id }}_cov
      SESSION_SECRET:        ci-test-session-secret-minimum-32-chars-000000000000
      APP_BASE_URL:          http://localhost:3000
      S3_ENDPOINT:           ${{ vars.S3_ENDPOINT }}
      S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:      ${{ secrets.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
      S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:  ${{ secrets.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
      S3_ASSETS_BUCKET:      ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BUCKET }}
      S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET:     ${{ vars.S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET }}
      S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL:    ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL }}
      OIDC_MOCK:             "true"

    steps:
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/share/boost /usr/share/swift /usr/local/.ghcup \
            "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY:-/opt/hostedtoolcache}" 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo apt-get clean 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h

      - name: Install required packages
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config postgresql-client
          # Note: libssl-dev is intentionally omitted — this project uses rustls
          # everywhere and must not introduce openssl as a dependency.

      - name: Create test database
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_cov;"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "CREATE DATABASE larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_cov;"

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0  # Required for accurate SonarQube blame data

      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: coverage

      - name: Install sqlx-cli
        run: |
          cargo install sqlx-cli \
            --no-default-features \
            --features rustls,postgres

      - name: Install cargo-llvm-cov
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov

      - name: Run migrations
        run: cargo sqlx migrate run

      - name: Run all tests with coverage
        run: |
          cargo llvm-cov \
            --workspace \
            --lcov \
            --output-path coverage.lcov

      - name: Upload coverage artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-lcov
          path: coverage.lcov
          retention-days: 1

      - name: Drop test database
        if: always()
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_cov;" || true

  # ── 2. Security audit ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Checks all dependency versions against the RustSec advisory database.
  # Fails on any known vulnerability in a direct or transitive dependency.
  security-audit:
    name: Security Audit
    runs-on: self-hosted

    steps:
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/share/boost "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY:-/opt/hostedtoolcache}" 2>/dev/null || true

      - name: Install required packages
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Install cargo-audit
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-audit

      - name: Run cargo audit
        # The runner pool's CARGO_HOME is on an NFS PVC (see
        # kubernetes/github-runner/readme.md). cargo-audit fetches the
        # RustSec advisory database via git, which uses flock on its
        # lock file — and NFS doesn't support locking. Override
        # CARGO_HOME just for this step so the advisory-db clone goes
        # to the pod's local fs instead.
        env:
          CARGO_HOME: ${{ runner.temp }}/cargo-audit-home
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$CARGO_HOME"
          cargo audit \
            --ignore RUSTSEC-2023-0071 \
            --ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0002 \
            --ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0098 \
            --ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0099 \
            --ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0104
          # RUSTSEC-2023-0071: rsa crate via sqlx-mysql (transitive, no fix available)
          # RUSTSEC-2026-0002: lru crate via dioxus/aws-sdk (transitive, no fix available)
          # RUSTSEC-2026-0098: rustls-webpki URI name constraints (transitive via reqwest/openidconnect; fix requires upstream semver bump)
          # RUSTSEC-2026-0099: rustls-webpki wildcard name constraints (same transitive path as above)
          # RUSTSEC-2026-0104: rustls-webpki CRL parsing panic — fixed in the 0.103.x line
          # via cargo update; the remaining 0.101.7 path comes from reqwest 0.11 (oauth2/
          # openidconnect) and rustls 0.21 (aws-smithy-http-client/hyper-rustls 0.24).
          # Both require major-version migrations of those crates to escape, so we ignore
          # it here using the same pattern as RUSTSEC-2026-0098/0099 above.

  # ── 3. Trivy security scan ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Runs two scans:
  #   a) Container image scan — checks the scratch image for OS/package CVEs.
  #      Because the image is FROM scratch with only a static musl binary,
  #      this should always be clean, but we verify it explicitly.
  #   b) Filesystem scan — checks the source tree and Cargo.lock for CVEs
  #      and misconfigurations (IaC, secrets, etc.).
  # Both fail on CRITICAL or HIGH severity findings.
  trivy-scan:
    name: Trivy Security Scan
    runs-on: self-hosted

    steps:
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/share/boost "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY:-/opt/hostedtoolcache}" 2>/dev/null || true

      - name: Install required packages
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config musl-tools docker.io

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl

      - name: Build container image
        run: |
          DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 docker build \
            -t larderly:${{ github.sha }} \
            -f ./Containerfile \
            .

      - name: Trivy — container image scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          image-ref: larderly:${{ github.sha }}
          format: table
          exit-code: '1'
          severity: CRITICAL,HIGH
          trivyignores: .trivyignore

      - name: Trivy — filesystem scan
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master
        with:
          scan-type: fs
          scan-ref: .
          format: table
          exit-code: '1'
          severity: CRITICAL,HIGH
          trivyignores: .trivyignore

  # ── 4. SonarQube analysis ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Uploads coverage from the test job and runs static analysis.
  # Requires SONAR_TOKEN to be set in repository secrets.
  sonarqube:
    name: SonarQube Analysis
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: test

    steps:
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/share/boost "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY:-/opt/hostedtoolcache}" 2>/dev/null || true

      - name: Install required packages
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y curl

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0  # Shallow clones degrade SonarQube blame relevance

      - name: Download coverage artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: coverage-lcov

      - name: SonarQube analysis
        uses: SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@v7.0.0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SONAR_TOKEN:  ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
        with:
          args: >

      - name: Bump version and push tag
        id: tag
        uses: mathieudutour/github-tag-action@v6.2
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          default_bump: patch
          release_branches: main

    name: Build and Push Container
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: create-tag
    if: needs.create-tag.outputs.new_tag

      # Free the ~30 GB of pre-loaded SDKs the GH-hosted image ships with so
      # buildx has room for the cargo target dir + intermediate layers.

          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet

          sudo rm -rf /opt/ghc
          sudo rm -rf "/usr/local/share/boost"

      - name: Log in to Container Registry

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx

        with:

          tags: |

            type=raw,value=${{ needs.create-tag.outputs.new_tag }}

        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          file: ./Containerfile
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          annotations: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.annotations }}
          # Two-tier cache: GHA cache is fast for in-month rebuilds, registry

          cache-from: |

# GitHub self-hosted runners (ARC)

Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners for personal repos, deployed via the
[Actions Runner Controller](https://github.com/actions/actions-runner-controller).
GitHub Free for personal accounts has no organisation, so each repo gets its
own runner scale set (one Helm release per repo).

## Architecture

- **`arc-systems`** — runs the ARC controller (one cluster-wide install).
- **`arc-runners`** — runs one `AutoscalingRunnerSet` per repo. Each scale
  set is a Helm release of the `gha-runner-scale-set` chart and watches a
  single `githubConfigUrl` (the repo URL).
- Each scale set spawns ephemeral runner pods on demand. A pod runs one
  job and terminates. `maxRunners` caps concurrent pods per repo (currently 6).
- Runner pods include a **podman sidecar** (privileged) so workflow steps
  can `docker build` against `/var/run/podman/podman.sock`.

## Files in this directory

| File                             | Purpose                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dm-mcp-values.yaml`             | Helm values for the `dm-mcp` repo runner set           |
| `foxy-fabrications-values.yaml`  | Helm values for the `foxy-fabrications` repo           |
| `larderly-values.yaml`           | Helm values for the `larderly` repo                    |
| `cargo-cache-slot-claimer.yaml`  | ConfigMap with the slot-claim scripts (see below)      |
| `arc.sh`                         | Reference commands for the controller install         |

The PVCs that back the cargo caches live under `storage/arc-runner-*.yaml`.

## Installing / upgrading a runner set

```bash
# Controller (one-time, cluster-wide)
helm install arc \
  oci://ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner-controller-charts/gha-runner-scale-set-controller \
  --namespace arc-systems --create-namespace

# A repo's scale set
helm upgrade --install arc-runner-<repo> \
  oci://ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner-controller-charts/gha-runner-scale-set \
  --namespace arc-runners \
  -f github-runner/<repo>-values.yaml
```

Each repo needs a `github-token` Secret in `arc-runners` containing a PAT
with `repo` and `workflow` scopes (referenced by `githubConfigSecret`).

## Cargo cache slot pool

### The problem

The cluster nodes are tight on disk, so each runner mounts a per-repo NFS
PVC at `CARGO_HOME` to push compile artifacts off-node. Mounting the same
RWX PVC into every concurrent runner pod creates a race: cargo's unpack
step uses `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` to write `.cargo-ok` after extracting a crate,
and cargo's cross-process locking (a `flock` on `.package-cache`) is
unreliable over NFS. Two pods unpacking the same dependency at the same
time — or a previous pod that died mid-unpack — produces:

```
failed to open `.../rustix-1.1.4/.cargo-ok`
File exists (os error 17)
```

### The design

Instead of all pods sharing one `CARGO_HOME`, the PVC holds a **pool of
N persistent slot directories**. Each pod claims one at startup, uses it
as its private `CARGO_HOME`, and releases it on shutdown. Caches survive
across pod lifetimes (warm builds), but no two pods ever write to the
same paths.

PVC layout:

```
/cargo-cache/
  free/
    slot-0/  slot-1/  slot-2/  slot-3/  slot-4/  slot-5/
  in-use/
    slot-2.arc-runner-dm-mcp-runner-abc123/   # claimed by that pod
      .heartbeat                              # touched every 30s
      registry/  git/  ...
```

Pod lifecycle:

1. **Init container `claim-cargo-slot`** (`claim.sh`)
   - Seeds missing `free/slot-N` dirs on a fresh PVC (idempotent under
     concurrent inits).
   - Tries to atomically `mv free/slot-N → in-use/slot-N.<pod-name>`.
     Rename is atomic on NFSv4, so at most one pod can win each slot.
   - If no slot is free, scans `in-use/` for stale entries (heartbeat
     older than `STALE_SECONDS`, default 180s) and `mv`s them back to
     `free/`, then retries.
   - Writes the claimed path to `/shared/slot` (an emptyDir shared with
     the runner container).

2. **Runner container** starts via `runner-entrypoint.sh`
   - Reads `/shared/slot`, exports `CARGO_HOME` to that path.
   - Spawns a background `while true; do touch $CARGO_HOME/.heartbeat;
     sleep 30; done` so other pods can see this slot is alive.
   - `exec`s `/home/runner/run.sh` (the GitHub Actions runner agent).

3. **`preStop` hook** (`release-slot.sh`) runs on graceful shutdown
   - Moves the slot back from `in-use/` to `free/`.

4. **Crash recovery via heartbeat staleness**
   - If a pod is OOMKilled, force-deleted, or its node dies, `preStop`
     never runs. The slot stays in `in-use/`, but its `.heartbeat` file
     stops getting updated.
   - The next pod's init container sees the stale heartbeat and
     reclaims the slot. No CronJob, no API access required.

### Why no `kubectl get pods` for liveness?

Earlier draft used the Kubernetes API to check whether a slot's owner
pod still existed. That works but requires giving the runner pod's
service account `pods: list` in `arc-runners`. Since runner pods execute
arbitrary workflow code, granting them API access is a security
trade-off. Heartbeat-based staleness is self-contained — the only
permission needed is what the pod already has.

### Components

| Where                                              | What                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `cargo-cache-slot-claimer.yaml` (this directory)   | ConfigMap with the three scripts                  |
| `<repo>-values.yaml` `template.spec.initContainers`| Runs `claim.sh`                                   |
| `<repo>-values.yaml` `containers[runner].command`  | Runs `runner-entrypoint.sh`                       |
| `<repo>-values.yaml` `containers[runner].lifecycle.preStop` | Runs `release-slot.sh`                  |
| `storage/arc-runner-<repo>.yaml`                   | The RWX NFS PVC backing the pool                  |

`SLOT_COUNT` (env on the init container) must equal `maxRunners` —
otherwise either some runners can never start (slots < runners) or PVC
space is wasted (slots > runners).

### Applying the pattern to a new repo

1. Make sure `cargo-cache-slot-claimer.yaml` is applied
   (`kubectl apply -f github-runner/cargo-cache-slot-claimer.yaml`).
   It's namespace-scoped to `arc-runners`, so one ConfigMap covers all
   runner sets in this cluster.
2. Create the per-repo PVC under `storage/arc-runner-<repo>.yaml` (RWX,
   `storageClassName: nfs`, sized for the cargo cache — 50Gi is a sane
   start). Apply it.
3. Copy `dm-mcp-values.yaml` to `<repo>-values.yaml`. Update
   `githubConfigUrl`, the `claimName` for the cargo-cache volume, and
   `SLOT_COUNT` if `maxRunners` differs.
4. `helm upgrade --install arc-runner-<repo> ...` as above.

### Resetting the pool

If the slot directories ever get into a bad state (e.g. you change
`SLOT_COUNT` and want to wipe the layout), shut the runner set down and
clear the PVC contents:

```bash
helm scale ...   # or kubectl scale autoscalingrunnerset --replicas=0
# Run a throwaway pod that mounts the PVC and deletes free/ and in-use/
# (leaving the existing registry/git caches alone if you want to keep them).
```

The init container will reseed `free/` on the next pod start.

## Operational notes

- **Token rotation**: the `github-token` Secret is referenced by
  `githubConfigSecret`. Update it in 1Password and re-sync; the runner
  pods will pick up the new value on their next restart.
- **First run after enabling the slot pool**: existing cache contents at
  the PVC root (`/cargo-cache/registry/...`) are not migrated into any
  slot. The first run in each slot starts cold. To preserve a warm
  cache, manually copy/rsync the old contents into one of the
  `free/slot-N/` directories before bringing the runners back up.
- **Diagnosing a stuck runner**: if pods are stuck on
  `Init:CrashLoopBackOff`, check the init container logs
  (`kubectl logs <pod> -c claim-cargo-slot -n arc-runners`). The most
  common cause is the cargo-cache PVC not being bound (check
  `kubectl get pvc -n arc-runners`) or the `cargo-cache-slot-claimer`
  ConfigMap missing.

# 1Password + Kubernetes Workflow Guide

## How It Works

The 1Password Operator creates a **one-way sync** from 1Password → Kubernetes:

```
1Password (source of truth)  →  Kubernetes Operator  →  Kubernetes Secret
```

You manage secrets in 1Password, and they automatically sync to your cluster.

## Creating and Using Secrets

### Step 1: Create Item in 1Password

1. Open 1Password app or go to https://my.1password.com
2. Navigate to the vault you gave the service account access to
3. Click **New Item**
4. Choose a type (usually "Password" or "API Credential")
5. Fill in the fields:
   - **Title**: `my-app-database` (this is what you'll reference)
   - **username**: `dbuser`
   - **password**: `super-secret-password`
   - Add custom fields if needed (e.g., `host`, `port`, `database`)
6. Save the item

### Step 2: Create OnePasswordItem in Kubernetes

Create a YAML file that references your 1Password item:

```yaml
apiVersion: onepassword.com/v1
kind: OnePasswordItem
metadata:
  name: database-secret  # Name of the K8s Secret to create
  namespace: production
spec:
  itemPath: "vaults/Production/items/my-app-database"
```

Apply it:
```bash
kubectl apply -f database-secret.yaml
```

### Step 3: Verify the Secret Was Created

```bash
# Check if the OnePasswordItem was created
kubectl get onepassworditems -n production

# Check if the Kubernetes Secret was created
kubectl get secret database-secret -n production

# View the secret contents (base64 encoded)
kubectl get secret database-secret -n production -o yaml
```

### Step 4: Use the Secret in Your Deployment

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:latest
        env:
        - name: DB_USERNAME
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: database-secret
              key: username
        - name: DB_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: database-secret
              key: password
```

## Field Mapping

1Password fields automatically map to Kubernetes Secret keys:

| 1Password Field | Kubernetes Secret Key |
|----------------|----------------------|
| username       | username             |
| password       | password             |
| Custom field "api_key" | api_key      |
| Custom field "API Key" | api-key (spaces → dashes, lowercase) |

## Updating Secrets

1. **Update in 1Password**: Change the value in your 1Password item
2. **Wait for sync**: The operator polls every 10 minutes (default)
3. **Auto-restart** (if enabled): Deployments using the secret automatically restart

To force immediate sync:
```bash
# Delete and recreate the OnePasswordItem
kubectl delete onepassworditem database-secret -n production
kubectl apply -f database-secret.yaml
```

## Finding Item Paths

You need the exact path to reference items. Here's how to find it:

### Method 1: Using 1Password CLI (easiest)

```bash
# Install 1Password CLI if you haven't
# Then authenticate with your service account token
export OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN="ops_your_token_here"

# List vaults
op vault list

# List items in a vault
op item list --vault "Production"

# Get full item details
op item get "my-app-database" --vault "Production"
```

The path format is: `vaults/VAULT_NAME/items/ITEM_NAME`

### Method 2: Using Vault/Item IDs

You can also use IDs instead of names:
- `vaults/abc123def456/items/xyz789ghi012`

IDs are more stable (won't break if you rename things).

## Common Patterns

### Pattern 1: Database Credentials

1Password item fields:
- username: `postgres_user`
- password: `secure_password`
- host: `db.example.com`
- port: `5432`
- database: `myapp_prod`

All fields become keys in the Kubernetes Secret.

### Pattern 2: API Keys

1Password item with custom fields:
- api_key: `sk-abc123...`
- api_secret: `secret123...`
- endpoint: `https://api.example.com`

### Pattern 3: TLS Certificates

1Password item with file attachments:
- tls.crt (file)
- tls.key (file)

The operator will extract file contents as secret values.

## Permissions

The service account needs appropriate permissions:

- **Read-only**: Can only read secrets (recommended for most cases)
- **Read/Write**: Can read and modify secrets (only if your app needs to update secrets)

Set this when creating the service account in 1Password.

## Troubleshooting

### Secret not appearing

```bash
# Check OnePasswordItem status
kubectl describe onepassworditem database-secret -n production

# Check operator logs
kubectl logs -n onepassword -l app.kubernetes.io/component=operator -f
```

Common issues:
- Item path is incorrect (check spelling, case-sensitive)
- Vault not accessible to service account
- Service account token expired or invalid

### Secret not updating

- Default polling interval is 600 seconds (10 minutes)
- Check if auto-restart is enabled
- Manually delete and recreate the OnePasswordItem to force sync

## Best Practices

1. **Use descriptive names** in 1Password that match your app/service
2. **Organize by environment**: Separate vaults for dev/staging/prod
3. **Limit vault access**: Only give service account access to necessary vaults
4. **Use read-only permissions** unless you specifically need write access
5. **Enable auto-restart** so deployments pick up secret changes automatically
6. **Use IDs in production**: Item/vault IDs are more stable than names
7. **Document your items**: Add notes in 1Password about which K8s resources use each item

# GitHub self-hosted runners (ARC)

Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners for personal repos, deployed via the
[Actions Runner Controller](https://github.com/actions/actions-runner-controller).
GitHub Free for personal accounts has no organisation, so each repo gets its
own runner scale set (one Helm release per repo).

## Architecture

- **`arc-systems`** — runs the ARC controller (one cluster-wide install).
- **`arc-runners`** — runs one `AutoscalingRunnerSet` per repo. Each scale
  set is a Helm release of the `gha-runner-scale-set` chart and watches a
  single `githubConfigUrl` (the repo URL).
- Each scale set spawns ephemeral runner pods on demand. A pod runs one
  job and terminates. `maxRunners` caps concurrent pods per repo (currently 6).
- Runner pods include a **podman sidecar** (privileged) so workflow steps
  can `docker build` against `/var/run/podman/podman.sock`.

## Files in this directory

| File                             | Purpose                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dm-mcp-values.yaml`             | Helm values for the `dm-mcp` repo runner set           |
| `foxy-fabrications-values.yaml`  | Helm values for the `foxy-fabrications` repo           |
| `larderly-values.yaml`           | Helm values for the `larderly` repo                    |
| `cargo-cache-slot-claimer.yaml`  | ConfigMap with the slot-claim scripts (see below)      |
| `arc.sh`                         | Reference commands for the controller install         |

The PVCs that back the cargo caches live under `storage/arc-runner-*.yaml`.

## Installing / upgrading a runner set

```bash
# Controller (one-time, cluster-wide)
helm install arc \
  oci://ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner-controller-charts/gha-runner-scale-set-controller \
  --namespace arc-systems --create-namespace

# A repo's scale set
helm upgrade --install arc-runner-<repo> \
  oci://ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner-controller-charts/gha-runner-scale-set \
  --namespace arc-runners \
  -f github-runner/<repo>-values.yaml
```

Each repo needs a `github-token` Secret in `arc-runners` containing a PAT
with `repo` and `workflow` scopes (referenced by `githubConfigSecret`).

## Cargo cache slot pool

### The problem

The cluster nodes are tight on disk, so each runner mounts a per-repo NFS
PVC at `CARGO_HOME` to push compile artifacts off-node. Mounting the same
RWX PVC into every concurrent runner pod creates a race: cargo's unpack
step uses `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` to write `.cargo-ok` after extracting a crate,
and cargo's cross-process locking (a `flock` on `.package-cache`) is
unreliable over NFS. Two pods unpacking the same dependency at the same
time — or a previous pod that died mid-unpack — produces:

```
failed to open `.../rustix-1.1.4/.cargo-ok`
File exists (os error 17)
```

### The design

Instead of all pods sharing one `CARGO_HOME`, the PVC holds a **pool of
N persistent slot directories**. Each pod claims one at startup, uses it
as its private `CARGO_HOME`, and releases it on shutdown. Caches survive
across pod lifetimes (warm builds), but no two pods ever write to the
same paths.

PVC layout:

```
/cargo-cache/
  free/
    slot-0/  slot-1/  slot-2/  slot-3/  slot-4/  slot-5/
  in-use/
